title: Design System: Fortuna · Master Your Money

scrollbar-thumb.note: Browser-chrome only (webkit scrollbar). Never render as a component surface.

app-surface-strong.note: Shares one value with app-rule-inner by design: the app world’s inner-register slate.

app-rule-inner.note: Shares one value with app-surface-strong by design: the app world’s inner-register slate.

display.purpose: The page-level claim only: one per major band, flush left on the 8-column side. (display-headline class.)

headline.purpose: Section titles under the 1px ink setting rule. (section-head class.)

title.purpose: Column and feature heads inside the three-thirds band. (story-head class.)

sheet-title.purpose: The in-sheet headline on auth pages: fixed 30px/700 at -0.03em, one per sheet. (sheet-title class.)

body.purpose: Paragraphs and decks; secondary copy set in Info Gray at 1.7 line-height.

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-labels: figcaption tags, header nav, notices caption, copyright, auth sheet caption tags and field captions. (small-label class.)

wordmark.purpose: The Fortuna logotype: header 1.5rem, footer 1.1rem, always 700 at -0.03em. (wordmark class.)

app-page-title.purpose: The one headline per signed-in page, Inter 600 at 24px and −0.02em. (sheet-title class in the app world.)

app-figure.purpose: Headline money in the figure cards: Inter 600, 26px, tabular. (figure-value class; the display register of the app world.)

app-heading.purpose: Sheet captions and card heads at Inter 600 / 15px.

app-body.purpose: The app world’s working copy: 14px/1.6; notes 13px, foot notes 12.5px, both in Secondary Slate.

app-label.purpose: Uppercase 11px/600 micro-labels: figure-card metric names, notice flags, footer, top-bar date. (small-label class in the app world.)

shadows.name: app-field-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Boxed-field focus ring in the app world: a state indicator that replaces the outline, never elevation.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: The only motion in the system, in both worlds: button and control backgrounds, quiet-link color and underline on hover.

motion.name: entrance
motion.purpose: Deliberate Flat Stability: the first painted frame is the final state in both worlds; the app’s ApexCharts charts ship with animations disabled.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Shipped kill switch in both shells (welcome/guest and layouts/app.blade.php); honor it even if future motion is added.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Swiss Light: deck and action rows inline; header "Log in" hides below it. App: records switch from stacked rows to the table; figure grids step to 2 across.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Swiss Light: 12-column grids engage; section headroom steps pt-16 → pt-24. App: top-bar date appears; content padding steps to py-12.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Swiss Light: forces the display headline’s two-line break. App: sidebar appears and the mobile menu control disappears; charts go two-up.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: App: the dashboard figure row steps to four across.

narrative.overview:
Fortuna looks like a Swiss typographic report: flat, gridded, unhurried, and precise. Nothing floats, nothing glows, nothing bounces. Every claim sits flush-left against a near-white paper ground (#FAFAF8), separated by hairline rules rather than boxed into cards, set in one grotesque family (Archivo) at tighter tracking as sizes grow. This is deliberate contrast with the hero-over-card-row conversion template the product refuses; the persuasion job is done by an inset specimen ledger table (hairline-ruled, tabular numerals, one overshoot flagged in the accent) because in this world an honest, well-set table is more persuasive than a testimonial could ever be (no testimonials exist, and none may be invented).

Trust is carried by restraint: shallow-gray secondary text, generous whitespace, one strong signal accent rationed to actions and flags, and data that always reports straight. The page is stable and flat by design: there is no entrance animation; the first painted frame is the final state. Since the first recording, the world has grown from the front page to the signed-out family: the auth pages are the same ground and hairlines with one specimen sheet where the front page sets a report.

Since 2026-10-17 the product deliberately runs two worlds. The signed-in family was rebuilt in Swiss Minimal Light, the world the user pinned: a white ground, #F8FAFC tinted panels inside 1px #E2E8F0 frames, Inter with tabular money, and one accent — banking blue #2563EB — running as a single thread per region (active nav, primary actions, meter fills, the expense line). It is the same restraint in a workday register: no shadows at rest, structure drawn at 1px, green and red kept strictly as state flags on data. The signed-in app refuses the generic gradient analytics dashboard; the ruled budget check stays the hero, and the four figure cards and charts serve it. Welcome and auth keep Swiss Light unchanged: the two worlds are a committed product decision, not a migration in progress.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white paper ground, pure-ink text, single strong red accent reserved for response (Swiss Light).
Hairline rules replace cards, shadows, glass, and gradient surfaces entirely (Swiss Light).
One self-hosted grotesque (Archivo, 400–700); display sizes track negative and set with `text-wrap: balance` (Swiss Light).
The working register (Swiss Minimal Light): white ground, #F8FAFC panels inside 1px #E2E8F0 frames, boxed controls at 8px, surfaces at 12px, Inter 400–700, 26px/600 figures.
One blue thread: #2563EB is the app’s only accent; green (#15803D and the notice greens) and red (#DC2626) appear only as state flags on data.
Tabular numerals (`.tnum`) on every money figure in both worlds, so columns align like a ledger.
Flat stability in both worlds: no entrance animation, no resting shadows; the only motion is 140ms state feedback, and the app’s charts ship with animations disabled.
Data honesty: numbers reflect stored truth; downloaded/announced features are labeled as notices, never shipped claims.
One sheet per signed-out page: the auth family repeats the front page’s paper, hairlines, caption tags, and single red submit (Swiss Light).
Two deliberate worlds, one discipline: a surface belongs to exactly one world (The Two-World Rule), and structure is drawn in both.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Fortuna Red appears only in response positions: the primary button, an active overshoot, a validation error, focus, and text selection. It is never resting-state text and never decoration. On any Swiss Light surface its total area stays small by design: that scarcity is what makes the overshoot, the error, and the one red submit read.

rules.name: The Hairline Doctrine
rules.body: In the Swiss Light world, structure is drawn, not built. No `box-shadow`, no `backdrop-filter`, no gradient panel, no rounded card. A container boundary is a 1px #E4E4E2 line; a section boundary is 1px #111111; row-versus-frame is two levels of hairline (#EFEFED inside, #E4E4E2 outside).

rules.name: The One Blue Thread Rule
rules.body: In the app world #2563EB is the only accent, and it runs as one thread per region — active nav, the primary action, meter fills, the expense line, focus. Semantic green and red never leave the data they flag. No second accent, no decorative fill: scarcity is what makes "past the line" read in red.

rules.name: The Two-World Rule
rules.body: Each shipped surface declares its world and stays in it: welcome and auth extend Swiss Light (Archivo, Fortuna Red, paper ground); signed-in pages extend Swiss Minimal Light (Inter, Ledger Blue, Working White). Tokens do not cross. Adding a surface starts by choosing its world, not by blending two.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any figure that means money gets `.tnum`, in both worlds. Non-aligned numerals in a data row are a bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The White-Out Rule
rules.body: The specimen figure and its ledger rows are typographic only: no numbered chips, no icon dots, no sparkline ornament. Attention goes to the numbers and the flagged row. (Swiss Light.)

rules.name: The Figure Register Rule
rules.body: In the app world headline numbers are set in the 26px/600 tabular figure display on the figure cards; they are never shrunk into chips, icon-decorated, or animated. Row money stays 13–14px `.tnum`; the display register is reserved for the month’s standing.

rules.name: The One Sheet Rule
rules.body: A signed-out page is one specimen sheet centred on the ground (caption tags, headline, deck, hairline field rows, one full-bleed accent submit, hairline footnote), with a single quiet cross-link under it. No split hero, no side panel, no second card; if the content doesn’t fit one sheet, it isn’t an auth page. (Swiss Light.)

rules.name: The Figures-First Rule
rules.body: A signed-in page opens with its standing as figures: the dashboard’s four cards (total balance, income this month, spent this month, budget remaining) sit above the budget check, and the charts sit below it. Those numbers are server-rendered, so the first painted frame is the answer; the check comes next, the evidence after. (Swiss Minimal Light.)

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift, in either world. If something must feel separate, separate it with a rule or a tone step (#FFFFFF on #FAFAF8 in the report; #F8FAFC on #FFFFFF in the app). Shadows are not in the vocabulary; a hover may deepen color, never cast.

rules.name: The Flat Stability Rule
rules.body: Swiss Light surfaces do not animate in. By design, the first painted frame is the final state: no entrance transitions, no reveal effects, no scroll-driven movement. The only motion in the system is responsive state feedback (140ms ease-out on hover of buttons/links) and the reduced-motion kill switch (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { transition: none !important; } }`, shipped in both shells). Stability here is an honesty signal: numbers first, presentation stable. The app world keeps the rule — its figures are server-rendered and its ApexCharts charts ship with animations disabled.

rules.name: The Only Float Rule
rules.body: In the app world exactly one thing floats: the dialog sheet, over a 40% Slate Ink scrim. It separates itself by the scrim and by focus — never by shadow, blur, or a lift.

dos: Do set every money figure with `.tnum` (tabular numerals) in both worlds, so ledger columns align.
Do keep each surface in exactly one world (The Two-World Rule): welcome and auth extend Swiss Light; every signed-in page extends Swiss Minimal Light.
Do ration the accent per world: Fortuna Red only for response positions in Swiss Light; one blue thread (#2563EB) per region in the app, with green and red kept as state flags on data.

Do separate surfaces by drawing them: #EFEFED inside a frame, #E4E4E2 between frames, 1px #111111 above headings, 2px ink under the header (Swiss Light); 1px #E2E8F0 frames and #F1F5F9 inner rows (app). That’s the whole hierarchy toolkit in both worlds.

Do keep each world’s typographic habits: Archivo’s negative tracking (−0.02 to −0.035em) and `text-wrap: balance` on Swiss Light headline classes; Inter with 26px/600 tabular figure cards and one hierarchy step per role in the app.
Do keep the specimen table honest: label it "SPECIMEN" / "Illustrative data"; roadmap items go in the "In later editions" list as notices, never as shipped claims.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (both shells ship the kill switch: all transitions disabled) even if future motion is added.

Do build each signed-out page as one specimen sheet on the ground: caption tags, headline, deck, hairline field rows, one full-bleed accent submit, hairline footnote, one quiet cross-link below (The One Sheet Rule), and put each error in the field row it belongs to.

Do make app dialogs modal in behavior as well as looks: `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"`, focus moved to the first field on open, Escape to close, Tab trapped inside, focus returned to the trigger — the shipped `layouts/app.blade.php` script is the contract.
Do cap the app meter fill at 100%: past the line, the red amount and the "past the line" note carry the excess, not a bar that overruns its track.
donts: Don’t introduce `box-shadow`, `backdrop-filter`, gradient panels, or glass as a visible surface treatment anywhere; flat-with-frames is the committed vocabulary of both worlds, not an early-stage limitation. The only sanctioned `box-shadow` uses in the CSS are state and plumbing: `box-shadow: none` suppressions (both worlds), Chrome’s autofill white-inset repaint (both worlds), and the app field’s 3px `rgba(37,99,235,0.15)` focus ring — a focus state, never elevation.

Don’t round corners in the Swiss Light world: 0px radius everywhere; the scrollbar thumb’s 8px is chrome-only. And don’t sharpen the app world either — 8px controls and 12px surfaces are its language. Geometry never crosses worlds (The Two-World Rule).
Don’t add entrance or scroll animations to any surface: the first painted frame is the final state in both worlds, and the app’s chart animations stay disabled (The Flat Stability Rule).
Don’t use an accent on gray text, resting numerals, or decoration — in either world. Scarcity is what makes the one blue thread and the red flag read.
Don’t fabricate proof: no testimonials, no invented user counts, no benchmarks or guarantees; the specimen ledger table is the proof component.
Don’t add a second type family to a world: Archivo carries Swiss Light, Inter carries the app; data legibility comes from `.tnum`, not a mono face.
Don’t mix worlds on one page — no blue in the auth sheet, no Fortuna Red in the app, no rounded 12px cards in the report, no 0px corners in the app.

Don’t inherit the stock Breeze leftovers (`x-header`, `x-modal`, `x-nav-link`, the dropdowns, the starter buttons/inputs, `layouts/navigation.blade.php`): referenced by no view, styled by an older starter, scaffolding rather than precedent.
Don’t let semantic colors decorate the app: green marks income, red marks overshoots and errors, and neither marks anything else.
